message.content:
Arthur Penhaligon was a man defined by his invisibility. Born into a family of modest means in a town that time had forgotten, Arthur spent his youth as the quintessential "background character." He was the boy who sat in the middle row, the employee who was never invited to the office birthday cake, and the neighbor whose name no one could quite recall.

Arthur didn’t mind the anonymity at first. He found a quiet comfort in being a ghost. He worked as a data entry clerk for a mid-sized insurance firm, a job that required him to stare at thousands of names, addresses, and social security numbers—the digital skeletons of other people’s lives.

The shift began on a rainy Tuesday in November. Arthur was processing a stack of archived files when he came across the folder of a man named Elias Thorne. Elias was everything Arthur was not: a high-flying venture capitalist with a sprawling estate, a collection of vintage cars, and a life that seemed to vibrate with purpose.
